verses.text: Then Hannah prayed: "My heart is full of joy in the LORD. The LORD has made me strong. I can laugh at my enemies, because I am glad that you have saved me.
No one is holy like the LORD. There is no one besides you. There is no rock like our God.
Stop your proud talk. Do not let arrogant words come from your mouth. The LORD is a God who knows everything, and he weighs what people do.
The bows of the mighty warriors are broken, but those who stumbled are given strength.
Those who had plenty now work for food, but those who were hungry are hungry no more. The woman who could not have children has given birth to seven, but the woman with many sons pines away.
The LORD brings death and gives life. He brings people down to the grave and raises them up.
The LORD makes some poor and some rich. He brings some down and lifts others up.

He lifts the poor from the dust and raises the needy from the rubbish heap. He seats them with princes and gives them a place of honour. The foundations of the earth belong to the LORD, and on them he has set the world.
He will guard the steps of his faithful people, but the wicked will be silenced in darkness. No one wins by their own strength.
Those who oppose the LORD will be broken to pieces. He will thunder against them from heaven. The LORD will judge the whole earth. He will give strength to his king and make his chosen one strong."
Then Elkanah went home to Ramah, but the boy stayed and served the LORD under Eli the priest.
Eli's sons were wicked men. They had no respect for the LORD.
This was how the priests treated the people: whenever anyone offered a sacrifice, the priest's servant would come while the meat was boiling, holding a three-pronged fork.
He would stab it into the pan or kettle or pot, and the priest would take for himself whatever the fork brought up. They did this to all the Israelites who came to Shiloh.
Even before the fat was burned, the priest's servant would come and say to the person offering the sacrifice, "Give the priest some meat to roast. He will not take boiled meat from you, only raw."
If the person said to him, "Let the fat be burned first, and then take whatever you want," the servant would answer, "No, give it to me now. If you do not, I will take it by force."
The sin of these young men was very great in the LORD's eyes, because they treated the LORD's offering with contempt.
But Samuel served before the LORD. He was a boy wearing a linen ephod, a priest's vest.
Each year his mother made him a little robe and took it to him when she went up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.
Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife, saying, "May the LORD give you children by this woman to take the place of the one she prayed for and gave to the LORD." Then they would go home.
And the LORD was kind to Hannah. She became pregnant and gave birth to three sons and two daughters. Meanwhile, the boy Samuel grew up in the presence of the LORD.
Now Eli was very old. He heard about everything his sons were doing to all Israel, and how they slept with the women who served at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
So he said to them, "Why do you do such things? I hear from all the people about the evil things you are doing.
No, my sons. The report I hear spreading among the LORD's people is not good. You are leading them into sin.

If one person sins against another, God may help settle it. But if someone sins against the LORD, who will speak for them?" But his sons did not listen to their father, because the LORD had decided to put them to death.
And the boy Samuel kept growing, and he was liked more and more by the LORD and by the people.
Then a man of God came to Eli and said to him, "This is what the LORD says: 'Did I not clearly show myself to your ancestor's family when they were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt?

I chose your ancestor out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to go up to my altar, to burn incense, and to wear an ephod before me. I also gave your ancestor's family all the food offerings the Israelites burn.

So why do you treat with contempt the sacrifices and offerings I commanded for my house? Why do you honour your sons more than me by making yourselves fat on the best parts of every offering made by my people Israel?'

So the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'I did promise that your family would serve me as priests forever.' But now the LORD says: 'Never again! I will honour those who honour me, but those who despise me will be treated with contempt.
The time is coming when I will cut short your strength and the strength of your family, so that no one in your family will live to old age.
You will see trouble in my house. Even though good things will be done for Israel, no one in your family will ever live to old age.
Every one of you that I do not cut off from serving at my altar will only bring tears to your eyes and sadness to your heart. All your descendants will die in the prime of life.
What happens to your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, will be a sign to you: they will both die on the same day.
I will raise up for myself a faithful priest, who will do what is in my heart and mind. I will give him a family that lasts, and they will serve my chosen king forever.
Then everyone left in your family will come and bow down before him for a piece of silver and a loaf of bread. They will beg, "Please give me some priestly work so I can have food to eat."'"
